To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(a) a simple CNN architecture is sufficient to obtain results comparable with state of the art, (b) the CNN architecture for speaker clustering is similar to that for speaker identification, but with different hyperparameters, (c) the CNN architecture is not sensitive to hyperparameters, and (d) the network trained for speaker identification can be used as initialization for speaker clustering, which is a significant improvement over previous work.
(1) CNNs are a viable alternative for speaker clustering and (2) that a CNN trained for speaker identification can be used for clustering with minor changes.

(1) CNNs can be used to perform speaker identification and clustering without the need for any handcrafted features; (2) the optimal design of a CNN for speaker clustering depends on the amount of training data available; (3) the best results for speaker identification are achieved when using the same amount of training data for the training as for the test data, whereas the best results for clustering are achieved when training on a larger amount of data.
